changes.after: NA marks a missing value. Comparing a missing number with two gives an unknown result, also written NA.

before: A mask from values > 2 selects elements whose comparison is TRUE. A comparison involving NA normally produces NA.
Indexing an atomic vector with an NA mask entry includes a missing result at that position. Unknown does not silently mean false.

is.na(values) returns one logical missingness flag per entry. ! negates those flags. Combining !is.na(values) & (values > 2) rejects missing entries while retaining known qualifying values. Both masks are evaluated elementwise: & is not short-circuiting, and FALSE & NA is FALSE.


```r
values <- c(1, NA, 4)
cat(values[!is.na(values) & (values > 2)], "\n", sep = "")
```
It prints:
```text
4
```

Complete local R example; the app itself does not execute it:
```r

cat(values[values > 2], sep=",")
```
